question: In the context of judicial precedent, which principle allows a court to avoid following a binding precedent by declaring it was decided per incuriam?
options: A precedent decided without consideration of a relevant statute or binding authority
A precedent that was overruled by the Privy Council
A precedent that has been distinguished on its facts
A precedent that conflicts with natural justice principles

question: Under the doctrine of promissory estoppel as established in Central London Property Trust v High Trees House [1947], which of the following is an essential requirement?
options: The promisee must provide fresh consideration for the modified promise
There must be a clear and unequivocal promise that strict legal rights will not be enforced
The promise must be supported by a deed to be legally binding
The promisor must have received an economic benefit from the waiver

question: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'ultra vires' in Caribbean administrative law?
options: A government minister acting without parliamentary approval on foreign policy
An administrative body acting beyond the powers conferred upon it by its enabling legislation
A court refusing to enforce a statute that conflicts with constitutional rights
A tribunal applying common law rules instead of statutory guidelines

question: In criminal law, the M'Naghten Rules establish a defence of insanity. Which element is NOT required under these rules?
options: The accused must have been suffering from a defect of reason
The defect of reason must arise from a disease of the mind
The accused must not have known the nature and quality of the act, or not known it was wrong
The accused must have been incapable of forming any specific intent at the time of the offence

question: The rule in Rylands v Fletcher [1868] imposes strict liability. Which of the following is a recognised defence to this tort?
options: Contributory negligence by the claimant reducing damages by 50%
Act of a stranger whose actions the defendant could not have foreseen or controlled
Inevitable accident resulting from normal weather conditions
The defendant's compliance with all relevant statutory regulations

question: Under the CARICOM Treaty framework, the Caribbean Court of Justice exercises which two distinct jurisdictions?
options: Civil jurisdiction and criminal jurisdiction over member states
Original jurisdiction under the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas and appellate jurisdiction replacing the Privy Council
Supervisory jurisdiction over CARICOM institutions and advisory jurisdiction to member state parliaments
Constitutional jurisdiction over fundamental rights and commercial arbitration jurisdiction

question: In contract law, which test is applied to determine the remoteness of damage in a breach of contract claim following Hadley v Baxendale [1854]?
options: Whether the loss was a direct and natural consequence foreseeable by a reasonable person at the time of the tort
Whether the loss arose naturally from the breach or was in the reasonable contemplation of both parties at the time of contracting
Whether the defendant subjectively foresaw the specific type of loss that would result from the breach
Whether the claimant took all reasonable steps to mitigate their loss before bringing a claim

question: Which constitutional doctrine, fundamental to Caribbean constitutional law, was articulated in Hinds v The Queen [1977] by the Privy Council?
options: The doctrine of parliamentary sovereignty prevents judicial review of Acts of Parliament
The separation of powers requires that judicial power cannot be conferred on bodies that are not courts in the constitutional sense
The doctrine of legitimate expectation binds the executive to prior representations
The principle of constitutional supremacy allows courts to strike down any delegated legislation

question: In the law of tort, the 'neighbour principle' foundational to modern negligence law was first articulated by Lord Atkin in which landmark case?
options: Donoghue v Stevenson [1932]
Caparo Industries plc v Dickman [1990]
Anns v Merton London Borough Council [1978]
Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd [1964]

question: Under Caribbean evidence law, the principle of legal professional privilege protects communications between a lawyer and client. In which circumstance is this privilege typically overridden?
options: Where the communication is made in the course of furthering a criminal purpose or fraud
Where the client has waived the privilege by disclosing the communication to one additional person
Where the court determines the communication is relevant to the central issue in dispute
Where the lawyer no longer represents the client at the time of the proceedings

question: The actus reus of murder in Caribbean jurisdictions requires an unlawful killing. Which of the following killings would most likely NOT be considered unlawful?
options: Killing by a soldier acting in excess of his orders during lawful military operations
Killing by a person exercising reasonable force in legitimate self-defence where such force was necessary and proportionate
Killing resulting from gross negligence during the performance of a legal duty
Killing by a person who honestly but unreasonably believed deadly force was required

question: In equity, the maxim 'He who comes to equity must come with clean hands' operates as a bar to equitable relief. Which scenario best illustrates this maxim being applied?
options: A claimant seeking specific performance of a contract who has himself breached a material term of that same contract
A defendant raising the Limitation Act as a defence to a claim brought after the statutory period has expired
A claimant seeking damages at common law after fraudulently inducing the defendant to enter the contract
A trustee applying to the court for directions having made an innocent mistake in administering the trust

question: Under the doctrine of parliamentary sovereignty as it applies in Westminster-model Caribbean constitutions, which statement is most accurate?
options: Parliament is absolutely sovereign and may enact any law without constitutional limitation
Parliamentary sovereignty is modified by constitutional supremacy, meaning legislation inconsistent with the constitution may be struck down by the courts
Parliament may only be limited by obligations under international treaties that have been domestically incorporated
The executive controls parliamentary sovereignty through the doctrine of collective cabinet responsibility

question: In the law of trusts, a resulting trust arises in which of the following circumstances?
options: Where a settlor expressly declares that property is to be held for charitable purposes in perpetuity
Where a trustee applies trust property for an unauthorised purpose benefiting a third party
Where a person pays the purchase price of property but legal title is taken in the name of another without explanation
Where a court constructs a trust to reverse unjust enrichment regardless of the parties' intentions

question: Which of the following correctly states the rule in Salomon v Salomon & Co Ltd [1897] and its primary significance in Caribbean company law?
options: A company may only be formed with a minimum of seven members to prevent fraudulent single-person enterprises
A registered company is a legal entity separate and distinct from its members, even where one person holds a controlling interest
Directors of a company are personally liable for all debts incurred during their tenure in office
A company cannot hold property in its own name where it is wholly owned by a single shareholder
